column1: # Every cache the plugin keeps (tests/backend/Users/UserCacheScan.cs finds them in the source) and why it can't serve a
# stale answer after a change to a user's access. Columns: member, build (both | jf12), class, key, reason (for keyed: the
# key builder Type.Method~text it must contain), rules. Classes: stamped = declared as Helpers/UserAccessCache.cs
# (fingerprint + version, race-safe); keyed = its key holds the viewer's access as the asking request read it; ticketed =
# declared as Helpers/WrittenStateCache.cs (state JE writes itself, on the ticket protocol); independent = doesn't depend
# on a user's access, for the reason given. Rules (';'-separated): write:<disposition> for a cache dropped outside the
# code that fills it (fenced=<generation>, locked=<lock>, self-keyed, own-state, per-call, disposal, evicts; never just
# "invalidated on write"); snapshot:<Type.Member>=<reader> for the one read by id a keyed computation may make (its key's
# own read, or a gate that answers only when unchanged); deadline:<text> for a time a store takes after its read that is
# not an answer's lifetime (a schedule, a back-off; round 5: an answer lives from when its read began, and a fence is
# sampled before the inputs it covers are read); note:<text> explains a keyed row's disposition. See
# Bridge metadata readiness: import and hydration state, independent of each viewer's access.
